email.body1:
John, saw Prove launch the Identity Platform and bring on the Anonybit founder to push deeper into biometrics.

A platform launch and expansion like that usually open more in-market accounts than the team can cover before reps ramp, and that is where deals quietly stall. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for Prove off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
John, quick follow-up for Prove.

With a new platform story going global, pipeline targets tend to climb faster than headcount can. Most leaders cannot say how many meetings they actually need to hit the number, so the gap shows up late and the quarter becomes a scramble.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I will walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings Prove needs to cover this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
John, last bit of proof for Prove.

Memgraph had more accounts in play than the team could touch and could not hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks with every email auto-logged to CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Prove's reply rate likely compares to other identity and fintech companies. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through it?
email.body4:
John, I will stop reaching out on this one, but did not want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling global pipeline without adding headcount is not a priority this quarter, no problem at all. Timing is everything right after a platform launch, and I know that stretch is its own kind of busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to an identity and fintech motion? I will tailor it to Prove either way.
